body: FORMAL UX AND ACCESSIBILITY REVIEW — BLOCK. Identity and scope: candidate cand-1NFG8CC1R6Z4H1SJTCC2VYFPRF at commit 34caf555d0b4137d3327c6d8db8783f631d1b653, tree 72300b4b435b98bb98f7fa3b62b13eb21b3fd13c, direct parent 84554a52a839d485e8c010c33c39f0de9169d594, base 003f12b. I verified the declared scope and reviewed every one of the 15 frozen PNG and HTML plates at original DPR-2 resolution. The manifest and fixture courts pass; pixels are exactly 2x the declared CSS dimensions; the supplied clipping, SVG text, text-overlap, label-mark, blank-band, active-semantics, fixture, Chronology, Feature, matrix, motion, and State Board checks are green. Blocking finding UX-B7, a regression of the former frozen-or-inert gate: the required FROZEN DESIGN SPECIFICATION — CONTROLS ARE INERT notice is visually absent on every plate. export.cjs lines 229-242 appends the notice inside the dark synthetic banner with background transparent and color inherit. Each banner leaves color unset while the body foreground exactly matches the banner background: 14 plates inherit #221D19 on #221D19 and Directions inherits #1F1D1A on #1F1D1A. Computed contrast is 1.000:1 on all 15 plates; original-resolution PNG inspection confirms that only the synthetic fixture text is visible. The current court at export.cjs lines 303 and 1319 tests only DOM existence, so frozenNotice=true is a false acceptance signal for the design brief requirement that inertness be visibly declared. PROOF-BOUNDARY.md also says the exporter adds a dominant notice, which the shipped pixels contradict. This is acceptance-bearing because realistic-looking controls remain visible while their non-operability is not. Required successor acceptance: give the notice an explicit foreground and background or set a suitable inherited foreground; prove its rendered bounds and WCAG contrast on every frozen plate; add a mutation that makes the foreground equal to the banner background or otherwise hides the notice and show the court fails. Passing observations retained for the record: the persistent Codex, replaceable projection, and inspector hierarchy is coherent; exact source text remains 16px with 24.8px leading in primary, compact, and comparison workspaces and 32px with 48px leading in the 200-percent plate; Compact exposes the repaired 584 endpoint and all ten declared reachability checks; Reflow presents a usable 320-CSS-pixel-equivalent alternative; Chronology cleanly separates exact discourse, partial-order world, and exact recall clocks, shows the s01/s02 crossing, incomparable units, and distinct source, off-source, and Unranked recall marks; Feature scale-space distinguishes 9w, 25w, 61w, raw, selected, missing, and coverage states by line form, texture, label, and geometry rather than hue; Recall Matrix now has a separate ruled heading for every named off-source destination plus Unranked; State Board supplies written and structural never-confuse diagnostics plus a distinct failed-build panel; Grayscale and Motion preserve categorical distinctions and reduced-motion meaning without colour or travel; Tokens, Concept, Directions, and Renderer Gap are readable and the prior Tokens blank band and Directions missing-banner defects are repaired. No new clipping or mark-label collision was visible. Prior nonblocking notes remain: UX-N1 the dual Codex columns in Recall Matrix are still narrow, about 300px; UX-N2 Focus Order still calls the sequence twelve tab stops while the inspector fields and grouped controls describe additional Tab traversal, so implementation should resolve whether the count is top-level stops or every stop; UX-N4 Main claim rows remain dense at roughly 10px and merit usability testing. The earlier notice-overlap note is structurally repaired by moving the notice into the banner, but the new inherited-colour defect makes it unreadable instead. This review certifies only the static plates. It does not transfer to live focus behavior, accessibility-tree behavior, 200-percent browser reflow, runtime reduced motion, or provider-compiled Chronology and Feature behavior. No authorization or landing is granted.
